## Yielded on a hot-file collision, not dispatched — `pm:dispatched` rolled back to `pm:blocked`

`domain:spec` cross-repo lane, direct maintainer dispatch session `session_f95e3874-e532-4748-a921-044aa2752a2b`,
readings 2026-09-07T06:0xZ. objectui `origin/main` **`cdbc852e9`** (the card's reading was `0558e0f78`).

Maintainer authorisation for the dispatch attempt, verbatim (⛔ quoted, not translated): 「这个作为专题卡，你直接派发」.

### Why this card was NOT dispatched

The pre-dispatch targeted in-flight check found a **declared file-surface intersection**. objectui#7122 is
in flight — assignee `os-justin`, session `session_01BAZFhALsQsGqxui8sNqM8s`, branch
`claude/issue-7122-spec-pin-17-3-0` (continuing PR #7685) — and its claim comment declares:

> File surface: `pnpm-lock.yaml` · **`packages/types/**` (src, zod mirrors, `__tests__`)** · …

`packages/types/**` covers `packages/types/src/index.ts`, which is this card's entire target. Same-file work
serialises across rounds; intersect ⇒ yield. objectui#7635 rides the same branch as item 2 of that chain.

`Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#7122` added to the body so the unlock scan returns this card when that
chain lands, rather than leaving the constraint as prose nobody re-reads.

⚠️ **This lengthens the objectstack#16325 chain by one hop**: objectstack#16325 ← this card ← objectui#7122.
Reported to the maintainer in the same session.

### Premise correction for whoever picks this up

The card's `packages/types/src/index.ts:1106` is **stale** — objectui `main` moved `0558e0f78` → `cdbc852e9`.
Re-measured at `cdbc852e9`:

```
$ git show origin/main:packages/types/src/index.ts | grep -nE "export type \* as Cloud|@objectstack/spec/cloud"
1116:export type * as Cloud from '@objectstack/spec/cloud';
```

**Line 1116, single occurrence.** It sits inside a family of sibling namespace re-exports (`UI`, `System`,
`AI`, `API`, `Automation`, …); control on the same file: 15 `export type * as` lines total, so removing the
`Cloud` one leaves a deliberate gap that the changeset must name.

Consumer count re-confirmed **0**, with a firing control:
```
$ git grep -nE "\bCloud\.[A-Z]|from .*types.*\{[^}]*\bCloud\b" origin/main -- 'packages/**/*.ts' 'packages/**/*.tsx' \
    | grep -v packages/types/src/index.ts
(no output)
$ git show origin/main:packages/types/src/index.ts | grep -c "^export type \* as"
15
```
⇒ the zero is a real absence, not a dead pattern.

### State

`pm:dispatched` + assignee were set as step ① of the claim pair and are **rolled back in the same session**
— assignee cleared, label replaced with `pm:blocked`. ⛔ No half of the pair is left standing: no `Claim:`
comment was ever posted for this card, and no agent was dispatched.

Claim: PM direct maintainer dispatch (no numbered round — direct-dispatch channel); serial hold cleared
Session: `session_f95e3874-e532-4748-a921-044aa2752a2b`
Branch: `claude/issue-8225-drop-cloud-namespace-reexport`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-8225`
Domain: `domain:spec` (cross-repo spec lane)
File surface: `packages/types/src/index.ts` (one export line) · the `@object-ui/types` surface pin regenerated by this repo's own tooling · `.changeset/` (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: claude-fable-5-1` (= `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; mandated by clause ② below — removing a published type namespace from `@object-ui/types` — not by a path glob)
Clause-②: yes
Serial constraints cleared: the hold recorded in comment `5565861943` is **released on measurement, not on assumption** — see below. objectui#7122 closed/completed, its chain PR #7685 merged 2026-09-07T07:48:20Z. objectui#7635 is still open and `pm:dispatched` to `os-justin` on that same chain, but its real sites are disjoint from this card's single line (measured below). No other in-flight objectui card declares `packages/types/src/index.ts`.

---

Maintainer statement that prompted the re-check, verbatim (⛔ quoted, not translated): 「7122 已经合并了」.
Standing dispatch authorisation for this chain, verbatim: 「这个作为专题卡，你直接派发」.

⚠️ Dispatched under the direct-dispatch channel while the `domain:spec` seat post (objectstack#6017) has an
incumbent. ⛔ No seat was seized; the authorisation above is what routes it.

### Why the hold is released — and why #7635 being open does not re-impose it

The hold in `5565861943` was a hot-file collision with objectui#7122's declared surface, `packages/types/**`.
#7122 is closed, but its chain item **#7635 is still open and dispatched on the same branch**, so "the chain
landed" is not by itself enough. Measured on `origin/main` **`411a132c0`**:

#7635's declared sites are three `packages/types/src/__tests__/*` files plus the objectui-side extension members
`SelectOptionSchema.description` / `FieldSchema.rows` / `ObjectSchema.editMode`, and two sites added by later
cross-lane comments (`packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/spec-symbol-parity.test.ts`,
`apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`). Do any land in `index.ts`?

```
$ git show origin/main:packages/types/src/index.ts | grep -c SelectOptionSchema   → 0
$ …                                                | grep -c FieldSchema          → 0
$ …                                                | grep -c editMode             → 0
$ …                                                | grep -n  ObjectSchema
515:  ObjectSchemaMetadata,
516:  ObjectSchemaClientExtensions,
```

⇒ The only `ObjectSchema` hits are **different symbols sharing a name prefix**, not the `ObjectSchema.editMode`
member. That member's real declaration is elsewhere:

```
$ git grep -ln editMode origin/main -- 'packages/types/src/**'
packages/types/src/__tests__/object-schema-metadata-spec-derivation.test.ts
packages/types/src/field-types.ts
```

⇒ **Intersection with this card's single line is empty, and provably so.** ⛔ Nothing in `#7635`'s work touches
`packages/types/src/index.ts`.

The `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#7122` line stays in the body as the record of why this card waited — a
closed target reads as satisfied; ⛔ deleting satisfied edges erases the history.

### Premise re-check at dispatch time (⛔ not inherited — the card's own number is stale twice over)

objectui `origin/main` `411a132c0`. The card body says `packages/types/src/index.ts:1106`; comment `5565861943`
corrected it to `1116`. **Both are stale.** Now:

```
$ git show origin/main:packages/types/src/index.ts | grep -nE "export type \* as Cloud"
1120:export type * as Cloud from '@objectstack/spec/cloud';
```

**Line 1120, single occurrence.** Consumer count re-confirmed **0** across `packages/**` and `apps/**`
(`\bCloud\.[A-Z]`, excluding the declaring file), against a control of **15** `export type * as` lines in the same
file ⇒ the zero is a real absence, not a dead pattern. ⛔ Whoever works this counts on the tree in front of them;
the line has moved three times in one day.

## Contract-review-tier review: **FAIL** — one defect, already red in CI. Patch round 1 dispatched.

Reviewer: contract-review-tier subagent, dispatched by this PM seat because the seat does not hold that tier.
Target PR objectstack-ai/objectui#8360 at head `bdbdebf8`. Findings ⛔ not inherited from the dev report or from
this seat's earlier fact-check; re-derived independently.

### The defect — inputs → wrong behaviour

`scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts:215` is a floor pin:

```js
expect(specifiers.size).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(17);   // :213-214 comment: "17 distinct specifiers"
```

It guards `collectSpecSpecifiers()` (`:977-994`), which scans every ts/tsx/js file under
`packages/apps/examples` for `@objectstack/spec[/subpath]` string literals and takes the distinct set — a
guard against the scan silently going empty.

This PR removed the repository's **only** `'@objectstack/spec/cloud'` literal in that scanned tree. Distinct
count goes **17 → 16** (reviewer applied the same regex to the base and head blobs: the set difference is
exactly `@objectstack/spec/cloud`), so the floor fails:
`AssertionError: expected 16 to be greater than or equal to 17`.

**Not flake, and not pre-existing.** `Test (shard 1/4)` job `101780633203` is `failure` —
`Test Files 1 failed | 667 passed (668)`, that assertion the only red. Shards 2/3/4 green; the last seven other
PRs' shard 1/4 green; main's own red is an unrelated coverage-lane `check-vi-mock-specifiers` collapse. The test
file's blob is **identical on base, main and head**, so the PR is what moved the measured surface and the re-pin
belongs to it. `scripts/__tests__` is not governed surface.

**Why neither the dev nor this seat caught it**: the dev's local run was `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`,
whose path filter can never reach `scripts/**/*.test.ts`; and both of us read CI while it was still
`in_progress`. The reviewer waited for terminal state, which is the whole point of the step.

⚠️ Knock-on: `Run built-artifact pins (dist project)` (ci.yml `:791-792`, shard 1 only) was SKIPPED because the
failing step preceded it, so `packages/components/src/__tests__/page-header-action-ids.dist.spec.tsx` has not
executed on this head. It must be green on the rerun — required in the patch report, not assumed.

### Everything else PASSED, re-derived

| item | evidence |
|---|---|
| removal complete, nothing else taken | diff is 2 files; `index.ts` −1 export line, +3 comment lines; namespace family base/main 15 → head 14, the 14 siblings byte-untouched; the gap comment names **no** spec specifier (head tree: 0 code hits for the cloud subpath, 5 pure-comment hits; control `spec/system` 28 files) |
| ⭐ zero consumers | re-derived twice (head and current `origin/main`), with an **engine self-test first**: same tree `-E '\bUI\.[A-Z]'` ⇒ 0 vs `-P` ⇒ 2. Under `-P`: `Cloud.` member access 0 (same-shape firing controls `Data.` 3 files, `UI.` 2); named import/export of `Cloud` from `@object-ui/types` 0 (controls System 1, Data 1); star re-exports 0; namespace imports 0; `import('@object-ui/types').Cloud` 0 (control 2 files); a perl cross-line scan of import braces over 4106 ts/tsx ⇒ 0 (controls System/Data/UI 1 each). The only bare `Cloud,` in the repo comes from `lucide-react` |
| published surface | reviewer used a cheaper independent method than the dev's probe: `git archive` base and head of `packages/types`, build both, diff the emitted `dist/index.d.ts` ⇒ **exactly one line**, `as Cloud` 1 → 0, family 15 → 14, `as System` identical as control, emitted JS byte-identical |
| changeset | present, `@object-ui/types: minor`, states the breaking removal with no alias and no window. Bump level correct per AGENTS.md (objectui's own breaking changes take `minor`), mechanically enforced by `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` |
| the local red the dev dismissed | verified rather than trusted: `handler-keys-string-any-mirrors-7344.test.ts` blob identical across base/main/head; its anchors read files this PR does not touch; under `-P` the anchor file sets are identical on both refs. Genuine host issue, `#8361` accurate |
| CI accounting | **32** check runs (not 33): 28 success / 3 skipped / 1 failure. All three skips legitimately filtered (`Test (coverage …)` are `if: push`; `dependabot` is actor-gated), and the workflows that produced no run are schedule-, path- or merge-gated — ⛔ not missing coverage |
| governed surface | only `.changeset/**` and `packages/types/src/index.ts`; zero governed paths; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green |

### ⚠️ A small thing that matters more than its size

The changeset body cites the census "against a control of **15 namespace re-export lines**". That is the
**wrong-shape control** — the one that does not exercise `\b` and therefore proves nothing about the pattern
under test. It is this seat's original error, corrected by the dev, now propagating into the changelog. Fixing
it is part of the patch round: a bad control shipped as evidence is worse than no control, because the next
reader takes it as method.

### Also corrected in the patch round

The card's acceptance item "surface pin regenerated with the repo tooling" was answered as an absence. That is
right for `@object-ui/types`'s own **export** surface — and stating an absence rather than inventing a
regeneration was the correct instinct — but there **is** a pin on the spec-**import** surface: the very test
that went red. The patch report answers the item accurately.

### State

REWORK, patch round 1 of at most 2, same claim, same branch. ⛔ No ACCEPT, no ready, no enqueue.

## ACCEPT — objectstack-ai/objectui#8360 at `21b1bf51f`. Contract-review-tier verdict: **PASS**.

Reviewer of record for clause ②: the contract-review-tier subagent (this seat does not hold that tier, so the
clearance is not this seat's to give). Scoped re-review of the patch round; its FAIL findings are resolved and its
earlier PASS items were re-confirmed against a `merge-tree` of today's `main` (`9dcc54529`, 15 commits ahead of the
base it first reviewed).

### The check that mattered most

A floor pin re-pinned to the wrong number is worse than a red one. So the reviewer did not read the new constant —
it **re-implemented the counting algorithm**: extracted `SCAN_ROOTS`, the extension list, `SKIP_DIRS` and
`SPEC_SPECIFIER_RE` verbatim from the test plus `SPEC_PACKAGE_NAME` from `scripts/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts:48`,
and ran it over a `git archive` of the head tree and of the merge tree. Both give **distinct = 16 exactly**
(ui 252, data 150, api 32, contracts 27, kernel 26, automation 18, bare 17, security 16, system 15, shared 15,
package.json 11, ai 4, identity 4, integration 3, qa 1, studio 1).

⇒ 16 is a measured number, not a number chosen to turn the shard green. `collectSpecSpecifiers()` is byte-identical
to the pre-patch version, the assertion is still `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual` (not weakened, not deleted), and the
following `toContain` assertions are untouched. The comment names objectui#8225, the file the removed literal lived
in, the objectstack#16325 chain, and the previous value.

### The rest

| item | verdict |
|---|---|
| changeset census clause | fixed — now cites a **firing** control of the same shape and engine (`UI.` 2 files, `Data.` 3 under `-P`), replacing the 15-namespace-lines control that could not fire. Minor: it compresses two censuses' controls into one sentence; semantically sound, accepted |
| the previously-skipped dist pin | verified **from the job's step list**, not its overall conclusion: `Test (shard 1/4)` job `101810932838`, step `Run built-artifact pins (dist project)` **success**, 16:42:51 → 16:43:29 |
| zero consumers | re-derived a third time on today's `main`, the head, and the `merge-tree` result (4112 files) — all zero, engine self-test and same-shape firing controls each time |
| #8404's three local reds | reproduced on this host **using the binaries the tests actually spawn**, not the reviewer's shell aliases: `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 (8 probe parse failures), `/usr/bin/grep` BSD 2.6 printing `Binary file … matches` where the test asserts empty stdout, `timeout` absent. Genuine host reds; CI's four Linux shards green |
| governed surface | clean; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green |
| CI | **32 check runs: 29 success, 3 skipped, 0 otherwise.** The three skips are the same legitimate filters as before |

### ⚠️ A correction to this seat's own CI reading

Earlier in this card this seat reported "27 success / 3 skipped / 0 non-green". That was **read off a truncated
enumeration**: `gh api …/check-runs` without `--paginate` returns 30 of 32, and the response's own `total_count: 32`
was sitting in the same payload, uncompared. Paginated, the answer is 29/3/0 — the conclusion survives, the method
did not. Reporting a clean sweep off a truncated enumeration is exactly what the "compare the returned count against
`totalCount`, never report clean" rule exists to prevent, and this seat broke it.

### Step-3 exposure — the reviewer found no third counter

Confirming the sweep recorded on objectstack#16325 (comment `5573633299`): the two exports-map pins
(`:152 toBe(19)`, plus `:153` deriving from it, and `:608 toHaveLength(19)`) read the **installed** spec manifest,
are correctly left alone here (lockfile resolves exactly one spec, 17.3.0, whose published exports map has 19 keys
including `./cloud`), and must move in the spec-bump PR. The reviewer swept `scripts/**`, every
`packages/*/src/__tests__`, `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.mts` for `toBe|toHaveLength|toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`
of 18/19 near exports-map vocabulary and for every other reader of `@objectstack/spec/package.json`, and
enumerated each near-miss with why it is unrelated (i18n family counts, peer-comparison prose, plugin directories,
alias config; the three other manifest readers iterate dynamically with no count pin). **No third counter exists.**

⚠️ One non-counter it added, unverified and not blocking: `main` recently took `ab03bffae`, a gate that judges spec
member citations in published prose. Five files cite cloud-subpath symbols in prose (`packages/auth/README.md:220`,
`createAuthenticatedFetch.ts:106`, `marketplaceApi.ts:85`, `usePackageL10n.ts:6`, `PackagesPage.tsx:76`). Whether
that gate calls them phantom once `./cloud` is gone is for the spec-bump PR to check. Appended to the #16325 record.

### Landing

Ready + enqueue. `objectstack-ai/objectui` **does** have a merge queue — ruleset `11776024` (`main branch`) carries
rule types `deletion, non_fast_forward, merge_queue, pull_request, required_status_checks`. ⚠️ This seat checked the
**ruleset** endpoint this time rather than repeating the mistake it made on the cloud repo, where it read classic
branch protection, found no `required_merge_queue` key, and reported a configured queue as absent.
